purpose: Forecast held-out malicious network behaviour from fully benign histories using multiple future horizons instead of a single heterogeneous 4-minute binary target.
source: Official CTU IoT-23 timestamped Zeek conn.log.labeled scenarios
final_validation: locked; no final-validation family may be scored while V28 development is tuned

temporal_protocol.horizon_target: for each horizon, whether any malicious-labelled network window begins inside that future horizon
temporal_protocol.heldout_family_rule: all blocks with held-out-family history or future exposure are excluded from train/calibration/policy
temporal_protocol.split: deterministic one-hour block split inherited from V23
temporal_protocol.test_positive: fully benign history followed by the held-out family within 30-240 seconds
temporal_protocol.test_negative: fully benign history with a fully benign next four minutes

feature_policy.causal_adaptive_summary: V24 per-history median/IQR normalized network dynamics only

model.calibration: per-horizon logistic calibration using calibration split only
model.horizon_fusion: maximum calibrated probability across available 30/60/120/240 second heads

policy_threshold.global: 99th percentile of clean policy-benign fused scores
policy_threshold.scenario_specific: 99th percentile of clean policy-benign fused scores from the same scenario only when support >= 50; otherwise global threshold

claim_boundary: A pass supports multi-horizon forecasting of these held-out development behaviours from clean histories. It does not prove prediction of every zero-day attack.
